purpose: Implements Critical CSS Generation — heuristic PHP-based extraction of above-fold CSS with inline deferral, background generation via Action Scheduler, per-template storage, and admin UI toggle with status panel. Includes REST endpoints, daily cron regeneration, and React UI integration with suggestions navigation.
riskRationale: Solid architecture with correct brace-depth CSS parser, recursive @import resolution, and proper Action Scheduler integration. However, several correctness and UX issues remain: token-based selector matching produces false positives for hyphenated class names inflating output, first visitors experience FOUC due to unconditional defer stylesheet filtering, cache clearing leaves stale status transients, and the media-query rule parser uses fragile explode() logic vulnerable to brace-in-value edge cases.
breakingChanges: New wp-content/cache/wppo/ccss/ directory for storing generated critical CSS files
Two new REST API endpoints: regenerate_ccss (POST) and ccss_status (GET)
Daily cron hook wppo_ccss_regeneration for CCSS regeneration
New Action Scheduler hook wppo_generate_ccss for background generation per template

text: The Critical CSS feature is well-architected with a proper brace-depth CSS parser, Action Scheduler integration, and clean separation of concerns across PHP backend, REST API, React UI, and cron. However, 7 important and 6 minor issues remain across selector matching precision, first-visitor FOUC, cache/UIM data consistency, parsing fragility in media queries, and inline @import resolution. These degrade output quality and UX but don't make the feature entirely non-functional.

reasoning: Token_match produces false positives for hyphenated class names (e.g., .page-title matching .page-title-wrapper) inflating CCSS output. First visitors get deferred CSS without inlined critical CSS (FOUC). Cache clearing leaves stale status transients in admin UI. filter_media_query_rules uses fragile explode() parsing. Inline @import in <style> tags is unresolved. These issues affect output quality, UX consistency, and parsing correctness and should be addressed before merging.

message: Brace-depth CSS parser in parse_regular_rules() correctly handles minified single-line CSS, multi-line selectors, and nested braces — a significant improvement over the original line-based explode() approach.

get_template_hash() correctly uses template slugs (home/single/page/archive) via get_current_template_slug() instead of theme folder name, fixing the fundamental hash mismatch that made frontend inlining entirely non-functional.

fetch_stylesheet_with_imports() with recursive @import resolution (up to depth 3) and relative URL resolution in resolve_import_url() provides thorough coverage of external stylesheet dependencies including Google Fonts and plugin enqueues.

inline_ccss() correctly checks for generated files first, falls back to Action Scheduler job scheduling with deduplication via as_next_scheduled_action(), and properly uses get_current_template_slug() for hash computation.
get_status_all() returns template labels alongside hashes, making the admin UI user-friendly instead of showing raw MD5 prefixes.
open_ccss_settings is properly mapped to 'fileOptimization' in FIX_ACTION_TAB_MAP, making Fix-It buttons for render-blocking CSS and unused CSS suggestions functional.
The regenerate_ccss and ccss_status endpoints follow the existing REST pattern with proper permission_callback, require_once guard, and consistent send_response() format.

token_match() uses \b word boundaries which don't prevent false positives for hyphenated class names (.page-title matches .page-title-wrapper) because - and _ are non-word characters in regex. This inflates critical CSS with irrelevant rules from cascading matches on partial class/ID/tag names.
suggestion: Use full token-level matching by splitting selectors on CSS combinators and comparing complete atomic tokens. Anchor the pattern on the full selector token with its prefix character (., #) and use a lookahead that excludes hyphen and underscore from valid trailing characters.

message: defer_stylesheets filter is applied immediately when criticalCSS is enabled, but inline_ccss() only outputs the <style> tag when the CCSS file exists. For the first visitor(s) before generation completes, all stylesheets are deferred with no critical CSS fallback, causing a flash of unstyled content (FOUC).
suggestion: Conditionally apply the style_loader_tag filter only when the CCSS file exists for the current template. Add a <noscript> fallback in inline_ccss() that links the full stylesheet.

message: delete_all_cache_files() deletes the CCSS directory but does not clear the wppo_ccss_status_* transients. After a cache clear, the admin UI still shows 'ready' status for templates whose files no longer exist, causing stale UI state.
suggestion: Clear CCSS status transients when deleting the CCSS directory. Either use Critical_CSS::clear_all() instead of manually deleting, or call a dedicated clear_status_transients() method.

message: regenerate_all() calls self::clear_all() which deletes ALL existing CCSS files before queuing background jobs. If some jobs fail (network timeout, Action Scheduler queue full), affected templates are left without any critical CSS until the next cron run.
suggestion: Generate files in-place (overwrite) so existing valid CCSS remains if regeneration fails. Alternatively, use a tmp-file + rename pattern for atomic replacement.

message: get_sample_url() only handles home, single, page, and archive template slugs. Custom page templates (e.g., 'page-about.php') fall through to 'default: return home_url(/)', generating identical critical CSS from the homepage for different template types. This wastes resources and produces incorrect CCSS for custom page templates.
suggestion: Add a case for custom page templates: query a published page using that template via get_posts() with meta_key _wp_page_template and return its permalink.
suggestionCode:
default:
	$template_pages = get_posts( array(
		'post_type'      => 'page',
		'meta_key'       => '_wp_page_template',
		'meta_value'     => $template,
		'numberposts'    => 1,
		'post_status'    => 'publish',
		'has_password'   => false,
		'fields'         => 'ids',
	) );
	return ! empty( $template_pages ) ? get_permalink( $template_pages[0] ) : home_url( '/' );

message: filter_media_query_rules() uses explode('}', $body) to split rules within media queries (line 631). CSS property values can contain '}' characters (e.g., content: "}", data URIs with nested braces). This reproduces the same class of bug as the originally-critical CSS parser, producing truncated or invalid critical CSS within media queries.
suggestion: Replace explode-based rule splitting with the same brace-depth approach used in parse_regular_rules() to correctly handle nested braces in property values within media query bodies.

message: Inline @import directives within <style> tags are not resolved. While fetch_stylesheet_with_imports() recursively resolves @import directives in external stylesheets, inline <style> blocks are added directly without @import resolution. If a theme embeds @import url(...) in a <style> tag (e.g., Google Fonts), those imported rules are not included in critical CSS.
suggestion: After extracting inline <style> content, scan for @import directives, resolve their URLs, and fetch imported content using fetch_stylesheet_with_imports(). Append resolved content alongside the inline CSS.

message: defer_stylesheets() only replaces media='all' and media="all". Stylesheets without a media attribute or with media='screen' are not deferred. While WordPress defaults to 'all', themes can override this and some plugins enqueue styles without explicit media.
suggestion: Also handle stylesheets with no media attribute and those with media='screen'. Add a check for the absence of 'media=' in the tag and insert the defer pattern accordingly.

message: parse_regular_rules identifies @-rules (font-face, keyframes, import, charset, namespace, media) to handle them, but @supports, @layer, and @container rules are silently consumed and dropped — they match the '@' prefix check but are not output by extract_above_fold_css(). These can contain critical layout styles.
suggestion: Extract @supports, @layer, and @container rules similarly to @media: collect the full block, filter inner rules through matches_above_fold(), and include them in the output if any inner rules match.

message: generate() method is missing a PHP return type declaration (string|false). All other major methods in the class declare explicit return types, making this an inconsistency that could cause static analysis warnings.
suggestion: Add the string|false return type declaration to match the docblock and class conventions.
suggestionCode: public static function generate( string $url ): string|false {

message: clear_all() calls Util::init_filesystem() and stores the result in $filesystem but never uses it — the code falls back to global $wp_filesystem instead. This is inconsistent with generate_and_store() which correctly uses the return value.
suggestion: Use the local $filesystem variable instead of global $wp_filesystem for consistency with the rest of the class.

message: Cache::clear_ccss() is a public static method that is never called anywhere in the codebase. The CCSS directory clearing is already handled inline inside Cache::clearAll() at line 926-930, making this dead code.
suggestion: Either remove the unused method, or call it from the deactivation handler and from Critical_CSS::clear_all() to ensure consistent cleanup.

message: Redundant require_once of class-critical-css.php. The class is already unconditionally included in class-main.php which is loaded before Cron is instantiated.
suggestion: Remove the require_once — Critical_CSS is always available via class-main.php's includes().
